### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **36** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**62** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 27e0bd58489c8f5606674822a68f6250f4512871`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `recordId (4 routes)`
- **15** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **51** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 27e0bd58489c8f5606674822a68f6250f4512871` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7460fc4e542de72034a9b29c4836ff731db5db11` — the merge of head `5d2f5efda8f9745e9f9e5141fca6fdb0e72dfdec` into base `27e0bd58489c8f5606674822a68f6250f4512871`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7460fc4e542de72034a9b29c4836ff731db5db11 && git checkout 7460fc4e542de72034a9b29c4836ff731db5db11
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 27e0bd58489c8f5606674822a68f6250f4512871 5d2f5efda8f9745e9f9e5141fca6fdb0e72dfdec && git checkout -B drift-repro 27e0bd58489c8f5606674822a68f6250f4512871 && git merge --no-ff 5d2f5efda8f9745e9f9e5141fca6fdb0e72dfdec

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 27e0bd58489c8f5606674822a68f6250f4512871
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 27e0bd58489c8f5606674822a68f6250f4512871` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `5d2f5efda8f9745e9f9e5141fca6fdb0e72dfdec`
Local-runs: none

PR #28128, card #27577, governing ruling 6492000994 on #8345 (letter B). Read: the card body and both comments (claim 6498318163, os-dev-report 6523900499), the ruling, the PR body and its 11 files, the net diff against merge base `549203d0`, and the 52 check-runs on this head. Gates: 39 success, 13 skipped (path-filtered), 0 failed, among them Test Core 1-8/8, Build Core, every Type Check and Lint lane, Check Changeset, PR-body guards and Governed Surface Queue Guard. No governed path is in the diff: the `skills/**` line, the ADR-0144 open item and the #27193 blank-code class stay with the epic PM, as the card says.

### ① Derived judgments

- **409 finding `currency_mode_to_record`** (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, `detectDestructiveObjectChanges`): right. It fires when the next field is a `currency` field with `currencyConfig.currencyMode === 'record'`, the previous field exists, its mode is not `record`, and it is stored (`isStored`, the same storage predicate its siblings use). An absent previous config counts as `dynamic`, which is the spec default (`field.zod.ts` 667, `.default('dynamic')`), so unset to record fires correctly and record to record does not. A brand-new field never reaches it (`if (!prevField) continue`). It reads no row: the whole detector is a pure function of the two bodies. The finding lives in the existing issues array, so it answers as the existing `DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE` / 409 with the per-face `destructiveChangeRemedy`. The only call site is `saveMetaItem` Phase 3a, inside `if (!request.force && singularType === 'object')`, and it runs only when `readMetaItem` returns a `prev`. So `force` lifts it, it fires only where a previous version exists, and it never fires at boot, because code-declared registration never calls `saveMetaItem`. No other tree file lists destructive finding codes (no enum or client roster to extend), and `check:error-code-casing` is green. The message names the code field, the three consequences and the command with `--object` and `--field` filled in, as the card requires.
- **Backfill `backfillRecordCurrencyCodes`** (`packages/objectql/src/record-currency-backfill.ts`): right.
  - The code comes only from the operator: `options.code` is the only value written, and nothing reads `defaultCurrency` or `localization.currency`.
  - A bad code is refused before any read: `resolvePair` runs before `keysetWalk` is built, and refuses an unknown object (`objectNotFoundError`, 404), a non-record field (`recordCurrencyFieldOf`, the write guard's own reader; `INVALID_FIELD`, 400) and a non-member code (`isValueDomainMember('iso_4217_currency', code)`, exact spelling; `INVALID_FIELD`, 400, naming the code field). The spec makes `currencyField` a field declaring `valueDomain: 'iso_4217_currency'` (`object.zod.ts` 1897), so this predicate is that field's own accept-set.
  - Only rows with a non-blank amount and a blank code are written: the code-present test runs first, then the amount-blank test, both through `isRecordCurrencyBlank`, which is now exported from the guard module and aliased back to `isBlank` there. The guard and the backfill therefore judge blankness by one predicate, and an amount of `0` counts as an amount.
  - It is a dry run unless `apply === true`, and a dry run calls no `update`.
  - It is idempotent: every write turns a blank code into a member code, and the keyset walk over `id` is not disturbed by writes that leave `id` alone.
  - Writes go through `engine.update(object, { id, [codeField]: code }, { context: { isSystem: true } })`, the same call shape as `summary-backfill.ts` (line 412). The R1 guard therefore judges the touched pair, and `valueDomain` judges the code. One row's failure is recorded and the walk continues.
- **Exported objectql surface** (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`): right. It adds `backfillRecordCurrencyCodes`, `formatRecordCurrencyBackfillReport` and `recordCurrencyBackfillComplete`, plus five types. The package has the single `.` export, so `isRecordCurrencyBlank` stays internal. The changeset names it only as the shared predicate and does not claim it as an export.
- **CLI command** `os migrate record-currency-codes` (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/record-currency-codes.ts`): right.
  - `--object`, `--field` and `--code` are required.
  - It follows the `summary-nulls` shell one for one: the occupancy gate before boot, `--yes` or a TTY prompt for `--apply`, a read-only boot for the dry run (`deferSchemaDdl` + `readOnlyProbe`), the no-app-objects refusal, `refuseUndeclaredObjects`, the journal-mode note, the `--json` envelope with `errorCodeFields`, and exit 1 on failures. It exits 0 on truncation, the same as `summary-nulls`.
  - oclif discovers commands from `dist/commands/**/*.js`, so nothing needs registering. The two tree-discovered rosters gained their rows, and Test Core is green.

### ② Semver level

The changeset `.changeset/27577-record-currency-code-backfill.md` gives `patch` to `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/cli` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, and those are exactly the three packages whose published code the diff changes. The rest of the diff is test files. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no spec key, value or metadata type is added, removed or re-meant, and every body that saved before still saves (with `force` for this one switch, which is the ruling's own reading). AGENTS.md's rule that `none` takes `patch` therefore holds. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right: there are new exports, a new command and a new member registered on the existing 409 refusal face. That is the reading of #27339 review 6490309706 that the ruling adopts word for word. The PR body and the changeset carry the same two lines, and Check Changeset is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag** (os-dev-report 6523900499): a non-forced save of exactly this switch now answers 409 until it is re-sent with `force`. Answered: accepted. The ruling requires this 409 by name (item 3), and it names "B′ (backfill without the 409)" as not chosen. It is an acknowledgement on an existing face with an existing remedy, the same kind as `field_required_no_default`. It does not narrow what an author can write, so the `none` / `(widening)` declarations stand.
- **open_questions**: `[]`, nothing to answer.
- **should-fix S1, escalated to the epic PM**: the walk runs under the unscoped system context, so one `--code` is written across every organization's rows. A `dynamic` amount was displayed in each tenant's own `localization.currency`, so on a multi-organization deployment the codeless rows of different organizations may be in different currencies. The tool has no organization scope and no per-organization count to split them by. The ruling's text ("every row", operator-supplied, nothing derived) is what the diff implements. The module doc acknowledges that a mixed field must first be split by the operator's own writes. This is not a defect against the ruling, so it is not a must-fix, but an organization scope (or per-organization counts in the report) belongs with the open cloud-tenant reach item the ruling left for M3 or later.
- **should-fix S2**: `--code` is judged by a pure predicate, yet it is judged only after `bootSchemaStack`. That boot is DDL-capable under `--apply`, and the confirmation prompt also comes before it. The card's "refused before any write" holds at row level, and the message says "before the walk read or wrote any row", which is accurate. Judging the code before the prompt and the boot would also spare the schema work.
- **should-fix S3**: `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` gives each sibling data command a table row and a section (`summary-nulls` at 1304 and 1452, `activity-changed-fields`, `comment-parent-pair`), but has none for `record-currency-codes`. `content/docs/data-modeling/currency.mdx` says nothing about switching a stored field to `record`, the 409, or the backfill. `content/docs/**` is not governed, so a follow-up docs PR fixes both.
- **Noted, not a finding**: changing `currencyField` while staying in `record` (pointing at a new, empty column) also leaves rows codeless and raises nothing. That falls outside the ruling's condition (previous mode not `record`); it is for the epic PM to weigh.
- The cloud-tenant reach left open by the ruling, and the governed `skills/**` line, ADR-0144 item and #27193 class, stay with the epic PM as the card files them.

No must-fix.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-mzbmzo`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CbTZrFqRYNgjSaSbN5`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么：** 已有数据的 `dynamic` / `fixed` 金额字段切到 `record` 后，旧行有金额无币种码；新增 `os migrate record-currency-codes --object --field --code`（默认只报告，`--apply` 才写，只写「有金额、码为空」的行，码由运维给出），元数据保存这种切换时返回现有 409 `destructive_change`（finding `currency_mode_to_record`），`force` 放行。
- **为什么改：** 裁决 6492000994（B）：允许切换，但必须显式回填；R2 本位币换算无法换算无码的行，所以要在 R2 之前落地。
- **风险与回滚：** 码从不推断，有码的行从不改，坏码在读任何行前拒绝；写入走 `engine.update`，受 R1 写入守卫判；409 不读数据行，不加启动拒绝。三个包 patch。回滚即撤 PR。
- **先看：** `packages/objectql/src/record-currency-backfill.ts`，再看 `protocol.ts` 的 `currency_mode_to_record` 一段。
- **两分钟验证：** `record-currency-backfill.test.ts` 8/8，`protocol-destructive-currency-mode.test.ts` 7/7，`record-currency-codes.test.ts` 9/9；三组消融均变红。
- **需要你做的：** 无。不触及受治理路径，非 Tier H；席位翻 ready、入队。skills 一行与 ADR-0144 开放项 13 在席位的 Tier H 收尾 PR 里。

席位意见：接受。契约复审在本 head 上 PASS（上一条评论），无必改。

## 席位核对

**ACCEPT** · epic PM `epic:#8345` · head `5d2f5efd`

- 形态：11 个文件，+1273/−2；`@objectstack/objectql`、`@objectstack/cli`、`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` 各一处源码改动 + 测试；一个 changeset（三包 patch）；`Clause-②: yes (widening)` · `Metadata-protocol: none`；draft。
- 前提实测：merge base `549203d0` 含 R1 四张 PR 与 #27991；切换 409 只在 `saveMetaItem` 有上一版本且未带 `force` 时触发，复审逐行核对。
- 门禁 check-runs：本 head 52 个，39 success、13 按路径跳过、0 failure；派生门 65/65 退出 0（开发报告 6523900499）。
- 接受的偏差：一次未带 `force` 的这类保存现在回 409——裁决点名要求，非收窄。
- 范围外去向：S1（多组织部署上一个 `--code` 写进所有组织的行，无组织范围参数）→ 并入裁决留给 M3 的云租户范围开放项，席位在 ADR-0144 开放项 13 注明；S2（`--code` 在 boot 前判）与 S3（`cli.mdx` 与 `currency.mdx` 未补）→ 席位另开一张小卡进 server 队列；`currencyField` 在 record 内改指向不触发——裁决条件之外，记录在案不立卡。
- 落地条款：非 Tier H → 席位 ready + auto-merge；合并后 #27577 摘 `pm:dispatched`。
